Contamination distribution corresponding to careless responding

Source: R/utils_distributions.R
careless.Rd

Generate relevant quantities of a contamination distribution corresponding to (stylized) careless responding behavior.

careless(
  model,
  type = c("straightlining", "random"),
  target = c("extreme", "all")
)

Arguments

model

list of relevant quantities detailing the distribution of ordinal measurement scales, as generated by [get_model()] or [simple_model()].

type

type of careless responding behavior. Possible value are: - `"straightlining"`: randomly select a response category from certain target categories, then use the selected response for all items. - `"random"`: randomly select a response category from certain target categories independently for all items.

target

target response categories for the above types of careless responding behavior. Possible values are: - `"extreme"`: select only from the extreme two response categories. - `"all"`: select from all response categories.

Value

A list with the following components:

X, Y

each is a list with the following components detailing the distribution of the careless responding behavior:

  • `prob`: vector of response probabilites, shared by all items.

  • `mean`: vector of means of the items.

  • `cov`: covariance matrix of the items.

cov_XY

cross-covariance matrix of the distribution of the careless responding behavior.

References

M. Welz, A. Archimbaud, A. Alfons (2026). Quantifying the impact of careless responding. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/8fj6p_v2 .

See also

[get_model()], [simple_model()]

[bias()]

Author

Andreas Alfons

Examples

# generate model distribution
model_XY <- simple_model(prob = "centered", K = 9,
                         length = 5, rho_w = 0.4,
                         rho = -0.4)

# straightlining from extreme response categories
straight_extreme <- careless(model_XY, type = "straightlining",
                             target = "extreme")

# straightlining from all response categories
straight_all <- careless(model_XY, type = "straightlining",
                         target = "all")

# random responding from extreme response categories
random_extreme <- careless(model_XY, type = "random",
                           target = "extreme")

# random responding from all response categories
random_all <- careless(model_XY, type = "random",
                       target = "all")
